contexts.text: In all the high places of their pastures () = to be sustained from good; for high places, like mountains, = the goods of love.
I will open rivers upon the high places (). AE 118:3. Explained. ( = to give interior intelligence. AE 518:5.) ( = intelligence from spiritual truths. AE 730:24.)
[151a]. At one side of the city were two eminences... He said, The lower eminence is called the Parnassium, and the higher one the Heliconeum. Explained. CL 156:2.

The hill and the watch-tower shall be upon the eaves to eternity () = that there will no longer be any Church with them, because there is nothing but evil of life and falsity of doctrine... Such (there) dwell in deep places, and are covered over by hills and watch-towers... (There) also are many Hells... completely hidden by the lands, rocks, and hills above them, or by the hills and watch-towers, where there is grass...
On the high places () = in the interior man.
